transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-05 14:00 PT | Duration: 1:14 | Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood PM); Ronan, Lina, Priya, Diego (Sirenix)

Summary: quick handoff from product to integration, wanted to validate that our onprem refarch maps to Sirenix Synapse appliance and that marketplace listing artifacts won't break their air‑gapped checks.

[00:00] Ava Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then Ethan will go through the onprem refarch flow.
[00:12] Ronan Keefe: Hi yeah Ronan here, Lina, Priya and Diego are on. We are excited — we've been digging into the draft refarch you sent.
[00:22] Ethan Cho: cool thanks Ronan. I'll share my screen in a sec. This call is basically to confirm three things — packaging for the marketplace, network/egress patterns for an air‑gapped deployment, and KMS/HSM integration paths. Also we'd like to run a small perf bench on your infra.
[00:36] Lina Morales: Quick note, our Synapse boxes are 8xA100 per rack, NVMe local, and for compliance we route all outgoing telemetry through our egress proxy. Any agents talking back to Redwood would need to hit a customer‑owned egress endpoint.
[00:52] Ethan Cho: totally noted. The Redwood private agent supports reverse proxying and you can pin the control plane connection to a whitelisted IP. In the marketplace listing we include an "offline install" manifest that doesn't phone home unless the customer enables updates.
[01:08] Priya Singh: what about KMS? We use Vault + an HSM module for production keys, can't ship plaintext model encryption keys.
[01:15] Ethan Cho: yes, we have two recommended paths — integrate with your KMS via the Redwood KMS bridge (we have a Vault connector) or our HSM token pinning flow. Small caveat, some older agents have a different TLS stack so we test that before signing the listing.
[01:35] Diego Alvarez: Are there known issues with key rotation? Our security folks want automatic rotation every 30 days and audit hooks.
[01:42] Maya Thompson: We can support rotation; the pointer is that rotation events trigger a rekey for cached KV entries — that can cause a brief latency spike if the runtime refreshes the KV cache. We instrumented that in Dedicated but we'll add a note for the onprem playbook.
[01:58] Ronan Keefe: ok so add a caveat in the doc.
[02:03] Ethan Cho: yep will do. Next — quantization. We ran the 4bit flows on our generic benchmark but want to validate on Synapse kernels. Lina, can you confirm if you want int4 with fused kernels or standard GEMM path?
[02:20] Lina Morales: fused is preferred for perf but we're conservative; we'd like to test both: int4 fused and int8 fallback.
[02:28] Ethan Cho: perfect. We'll run both. I'll also instrument token latency percentiles and tail latency.
[02:36] Ava Patel: client asks about canary routing — if a model rollout fails we need to fall back to a hosted variant. How tightly coupled is that config?
[02:44] Ethan Cho: Redwood routing supports policy rules: you can set region/latency/cost thresholds. For Private we include a canary selector that routes a percentage to the local model and the remainder to a hosted fallback. That requires the customer's network to allow egress to the Redwood control plane for the fallback traffic (or you can use a peering proxy).
[03:03] Priya Singh: we prefer no egress. Is there a purely local fallback?
[03:08] Ethan Cho: you can configure a local smaller model as fallback — so local only, no egress. Tradeoff is accuracy. We'll document suggested fallback candidates in the refarch.
[03:20] Ronan Keefe: good.
[03:24] [05:00] Ethan Cho: dropping into the manifests — here's the helm chart snippet for the agent, notice the env vars for KMS_ENDPOINT and CONTROL_PLANE_MODE. (screen share noises)
[05:22] Lina Morales: the YAML has a liveness probe that assumes a loopback NFS mount; we use ephemeral volumes on Synapse. That probe will fail in our setup.
[05:30] Ethan Cho: ah ok, we'll provide an alternate probe config that uses a disk‑based healthcheck. We'll add a templated value to the chart.
[05:42] Diego Alvarez: what about resource pins — the container requests look low, will it tailspin under heavy batch loads?
[05:50] Ethan Cho: in our recommended profile for Synapse we double the CPU and give 1x extra GPU memory reservation for KV cache. The manifest will have a profile called "synapse‑large".
[06:00] [10:14] Maya Thompson: quick aside — packaging for the marketplace: we need a signed bundle (tar.gz) with manifests, RBAC snippets, and a validation script. Sirenix will want to run the validation in their CI. We'll publish a validation test harness in the repo.
[10:28] Ronan Keefe: can that harness run offline? Our CI can't access external endpoints.
[10:34] Maya Thompson: yes, the harness can be run in offline mode; it accepts a local mirror of images and a kubeconfig. We'll include instructions in README.md.
[10:44] Priya Singh: audit logs — we need per‑token audit trails for compliance. How much do you ship?
[10:52] Ethan Cho: Redwood ships audit events for request/response metadata and token counts; payloads can be scrubbed. For onprem installs we support local audit log ingestion into your ELK/FluentD, and we can optionally forward hashes to Redwood telemetry for billing only if you enable it.
[11:10] Priya Singh: that's critical, we'll default to local only.
[11:15] [18:22] Lina Morales: about network egress: we need a clear list of endpoints and ports.
[18:28] Ava Patel: Ethan, can you call out the list now?
[18:31] Ethan Cho: sure — control plane (if enabled) 443 to api.redwood.example, telemetry optional 443 to telemetry.redwood.example, license check uses signed tokens via the registry endpoint. But again offline install avoids those. We'll put a small table in the doc.
[18:50] Ronan Keefe: one more question on data residency: we may split EU workloads to a separate cluster. Does the marketplace listing support region labels so we can pin a model version to EU cluster only?
[19:02] Ethan Cho: yes, the deployment manifest allows a location selector label, you can restrict a rollout to a cluster by label. We also support per‑route SLOs if you want to vary latency budgets.
[19:15] [25:45] Diego Alvarez: benchmarking — what metrics should we expect? Throughput, p95, p99, and GPU utilization? Anything else?
[25:52] Ethan Cho: also include cold start time for the KV cache, token‑per‑second steady state, and token throughput under batching. We'll share our benchmark harness repo link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness (note: internal link)
[26:10] Lina Morales: please ensure the harness supports our local varying batch sizes, our token mix is chattier than normal.
[26:18] Ethan Cho: we'll add a script to synthesize short context dialogues.
[26:25] Ava Patel: competitor question — Ronan asked earlier about VertexServe; how do we position here?
[26:32] Ethan Cho: primary differentiation is the rollout tooling and KV cache transparency plus the marketplace packaging that supports offline, signed manifests. VertexServe has a hosted+edge model but their offline packaging is more manual. We'll surface that in the partner brief.
[26:50] Priya Singh: ok good.
[26:56] [34:00] Maya Thompson: action items recap — Ethan run perf, Maya publish manifests, Ava send checklist. Any follow ups from Sirenix?
34:05 Ronan Keefe: we'll confirm KMS details and send a sample PKCS11 config.
34:12 Lina Morales: and we'll try a dry run of the validation harness next week.
34:18 Diego Alvarez: can you also provide a sample RBAC snippet for our security team review?
34:24 Maya Thompson: yes, will add to the repo.

[47:10] Ethan Cho: small note about quantization caveat — on Synapse the fused int4 path requires a specific cuBLAS minor version; if their drivers are older we'll fall back to int8. We'll add a driver check to the validation harness.
[47:28] Lina Morales: we'll inventory the driver versions and share.

[57:02] Priya Singh: regarding compliance artifacts, can you share your SOC/ISO attestation docs? We need to attach them to our vendor review.
[57:10] Ava Patel: yes — I'll send the SOC 2 Type II summary and ISO overview, and point you to the security portal.
[57:24] Priya Singh: and do you provide an encryption whitepaper?
[57:28] Ethan Cho: yes will attach the KMS integration guide.

[68:44] Maya Thompson: last thing — packaging naming and versioning. We'll version the listing with a semver and include a digest for air‑gapped installs. That way you can validate install integrity without internet access.
[68:58] Ronan Keefe: great.
[69:05] Ava Patel: thanks everyone — recap in the notes, next sync week of 2027-10-18 for a deployment walk‑through. We'll send the artifacts off.
[69:20] Ronan Keefe: thanks all, bye.
[69:25] End of meeting.
